title: Claude plays Minecraft!
talk_summary: A demo talk about building a Minecraft-playing agent ('Rocky') using Mineflayer plus Amazon Bedrock Agents, with Claude Haiku as the model and 'return of control' actions. It is mostly a product demo of Bedrock Agents; the only transferable engineering content is the pattern of a strict JSON-schema system prompt for a complex generative action, and the observation that LangChain became too complex as tools grew.

takeaways.technique: Strict schema + rules prompt for generative structured output
takeaways.what_they_do: For the complex 'build' action they give the model an expert persona, the exact JSON format the client consumes, and an explicit rule list and block whitelist, because without the rules the model 'goes bananas' and emits nonsense.
takeaways.evidence_quote: then you'll go strictly adere to the following rules because if you we didn't do that it goes bananas uh and builds just nonsense

takeaways.technique: Drop heavyweight framework when tool count grows
takeaways.what_they_do: They started with LangChain on Lambda, but as actions and tools multiplied the code 'got really really complex', so they moved to a managed agent abstraction with declarative action definitions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as we had a complexity and more and more actions and tools for Rocky to use uh it got really really um complex

takeaways.technique: Small fast model for interactive tool-calling
takeaways.what_they_do: They chose Claude Haiku specifically for latency in an interactive loop rather than a larger model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Claud in in particular Claude Haiku because it's it's fast
